questions.q: What happens if you call pd.DataFrame() directly on genuinely nested JSON?
options: Entire dictionaries end up sitting inside single cells, instead of being broken into their own columns
Pandas automatically flattens it perfectly with no extra steps
It raises an error and refuses to create a DataFrame
Nested JSON cannot be loaded into Python at all
questions.explain: This is exactly why pd.json_normalize() exists as a separate tool for nested structures.

questions.q: How does chained key access like trip['fare']['amount'] work?
options: Exactly like Lesson 15's dictionary access, just applied one level deeper each time
It requires a completely different syntax from normal dictionary access
It only works after calling json_normalize first
Chained access is not possible in Python

questions.q: What is the relationship between json.dumps() and json.loads()?
options: dumps converts Python objects into JSON text; loads converts JSON text back into Python objects — opposite directions
They do exactly the same thing with no difference
dumps only works on numbers; loads only works on strings
Both functions delete data rather than convert it
questions.explain: loads parses text into Python; dumps serializes Python objects back into text.
